name: Tears and Scars
description: "Tears and Scars" is That Boy Hi Hat at his most confessional, and the catalog treats it accordingly: the identical recording appears on both Post Trap Futurism: The Logo Effect and Idol or Icon, preserved unchanged — too foundational to touch. At 4:40, the track takes its time. The title tells you the thematic ground — loss, loyalty, the cost of the road — and the performance backs it up with a melancholic weight that sounds like one take left alone. In the vein of the great late-night confessionals of alternative rap, the record is introspective rather than performative, vulnerable without tipping into sentimentality, a diary entry recalling the artist's loneliest hours. The sound is dark in texture but mellow in motion: piano tones drift over synth beds, ethereal strings swell with real depth layered underneath the vocal, and an 808 sub bass anchors the low end, giving every line room to land. Hi-hats tick throughout with restraint, vocal chops echo in the spaces between phrases, and ad-libs stay buried low, ghosting the lead as the sub bass pulses beneath. The minor-key gravity never brightens into anything major-key — the sadness here is performed for no one, just documented. The mix keeps the vocal forward and the grain intact, a studio-polished frame around a raw, gritty performance. For fans of nocturnal rap and dark trap, this is the sound of someone who has been through it: lonely, haunting, sad, honest. It sits in the catalog as the other half of the emotional ledger beside Rainbows And Roses, and in a scene where the current wave of cinematic rap keeps getting louder, few records earn this level of stillness. That Boy Hi Hat proves the hardest thing to do in post trap is not go harder; it is go honest.
